topics.title: What Social Science Is and Its Place in Everyday Life
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Social Science in Everyday Life

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Social Science as the systematic study of human society and how it differs from the natural sciences.
Explain how ordinary daily activities depend on wider systems of governance, economy, society and environment.

topics.title: Understanding Society through Time and Traditions
topics.ncert_sections: Understanding Society through Time and Traditions

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how human societies changed from early communities to villages, towns and cities.
Explain how ideas such as the Panchamahabhutas, vasudhaiva kutumbakam and the Arthashastra reflect early inquiry into society.
Identify the methods social scientists use to gather evidence and build explanations.

topics.title: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines
topics.ncert_sections: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a complex society must be studied from the perspectives of several related disciplines.
Identify the four core disciplines of Grades 9-10 Social Science and the wider Social Science family.
Describe what Geography studies, including location, distribution and human-environment relationships.
Explain how Geography combines spatial and temporal perspectives in a holistic approach.
Identify the tools Geography uses, such as maps, globes, atlases and GIS.
Explain the role of the itihasa-purana tradition in preserving cultural memory in Bharat.
Describe how modern historiography uses empirical evidence and scientific tools.
Classify sources of history as literary, archaeological, epigraphic or numismatic.
Describe Political Science as the study of governance, power, constitutions and institutions.
Explain how early Indian political thought linked politics with dharma, artha and rajadharma.
Explain how the Panchayati Raj system shows grassroots democracy and local participation.
Explain how Economics studies the use of limited resources and decisions by consumers, producers and governments.
Describe India's economic journey from a leading economy through colonial disruption to rebuilding after independence.
Explain sustainable growth as meeting present needs without harming future generations.

topics.title: Why Study Social Science and Its Future
topics.ncert_sections: Why Should We Study Social Science?; The Future of Social Science; Secondary-Stage Social Science

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how understanding government and shared challenges prepares students for responsible civic life.
Explain how Social Science accounts for diversity and the underlying unity of Indian society.
Describe the growing role of Social Science in addressing future challenges and linking past, present and future.
